project.name: spring-rest-sakila
project.description: The Spring REST Sakila project is a sample REST API service providing access to the MySQL Sakila database, a learning database that models a DVD rental store company. The service enables CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations and complex queries on data including films, actors, customers, rentals, payments, staff, stores, and location information. It demonstrates enterprise patterns and best practices for building a production-ready REST API with Spring Boot, including authentication, authorization, caching, and comprehensive API documentation.
project.architecture_summary: The application follows a layered architecture organized around multiple domain modules (catalog, customer, location, payment, rental, staff, store, and authentication). Each domain contains controller, service, repository, mapper, entity, and DTO layers. The repository layer implements the custom repository pattern with both Spring Data JPA and Querydsl/Blaze-Persistence for complex queries. Services provide business logic and transactional boundaries. Controllers expose REST endpoints with HATEOAS support. Mappers handle bidirectional conversions between entities and DTOs. Cross-cutting concerns are managed through configuration classes for security, persistence, logging, and caching. The application uses Spring Security with JWT-based authentication and Spring Data REST conventions for API consistency.
